cohort: The study initially selected 12,132 late-pregnancy pregnant women admitted in Shanghai from January to December 2022, from whom 210 GBS-positive and 200 GBS-negative women were randomly selected for detailed comparison.
finding: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) infection in late pregnancy was identified as an independent risk factor for neonatal infection.
mod_finding: The incidence of vaginal delivery was significantly higher in the GBS positive group compared to the GBS negative group, and vaginal delivery was included as an independent variable in the analysis for neonatal infection.
cross-section timing: The study utilized data from women admitted between January 2022 and December 2022.
